1.title: Branches and Tags
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Branches and Tags. It covers the exam area Part two: Branching and history. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Create, list, switch, rename and delete branches. Explain why git branch -d refuses an unmerged branch. Read git branch dash v v. Recognize a detached head and rescue commits made in it. Create lightweight and annotated tags. Read git describe. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Course
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the course. Part: Part two: Branching and history. Verified with: Git two point five zero.one: every command was run in the lab.

1.title: Create, list and switch
1.text: Create, list and switch. A branch is only a pointer to a commit (module one), so branches are cheap and you should use them freely. One branch per task keeps unfinished work away from main. The figure shows two branches and a tag in one history.

1.title: Create, list and switch, continued
1.text: Create, list and switch. The figure shows this: Branches and tags in one history: main and feature or search are movable pointers to commits, v one.zero is a fixed tag, and head marks the branch you are on.

1.title: Create, list and switch, continued
1.text: Create, list and switch. git branch. Lists local branches; a star marks the current one. git branch name. Creates a branch and stays where you are. git switch name. Moves to an existing branch. git switch dash c name. Creates a branch and moves to it. git switch -. Returns to the previous branch. git switch dash c name start. Creates it at another commit or branch. Older guides use git checkout name to switch and git checkout dash b name to create and switch. They still work. git checkout also restores files, which is why Git added the clearer switch and restore.

1.title: Create, list and switch, continued
1.text: Create, list and switch. A slash in a name, as in feature slash search, is fine and makes a nested pointer file. A space is not allowed. Switching rewrites the files in your folder to match the other branch. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create, list and switch, continued
1.text: Create, list and switch. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create, list and switch, continued
1.text: Create, list and switch. Uncommitted edits travel with you when the file is identical in both branches. If switching would overwrite your edit, Git stops and says the local changes would be overwritten. You stay where you are and nothing is lost. Tip: Commit your work before you switch branches. Uncommitted edits either travel with you or block the switch, and both surprise people.

1.title: Rename, delete and inspect
1.text: Rename, delete and inspect. git branch dash m old new renames a branch, and git branch dash m new renames the current one. Renaming moves the pointer file, and the commits stay as they are. Deleting has two flags. dash d. Safe: refuses a branch that has commits not merged into your current branch. dash D. Forced: deletes the branch whatever it holds. You cannot delete the branch you are on. git branch the merged flag and git branch the no merged flag list branches by that test. Your hashes will differ from the ones in this module. The next block assumes that feature slash search has one commit that main lacks.

1.text: Rename, delete and inspect. In the output below, origin slash main ahead one means main has one commit that origin does not have yet (module seven). A branch with no upstream shows no brackets.

1.title: Detached HEAD
1.text: Detached head. Normally head holds a branch name. When you check out a commit hash or a tag, head holds the raw hash instead. This is a detached head. It is fine for looking around or building an old release. git status says "head detached at" and git branch marks it. Git prints a long advice message when you detach, which names git switch dash c. The block below leaves it out. git switch - or git switch main leaves the detached state.

1.title: Detached HEAD, continued
1.text: Detached head. The danger is a commit made there. It belongs to no branch, so after you switch away nothing points to it, and it can be lost when Git cleans up. The commit does still exist for a while: git branch rescue hash brings it back if you know the hash. Better, rescue it while you are still there with git switch dash c.

1.title: Detached HEAD, continued
1.text: Detached head. The commit made while detached is now safe on the rescue branch, and head is attached again. Tip: If git status says head detached and you made commits, run git switch dash c name before you leave. The branch name is what keeps the commits reachable.

1.title: Tags
1.text: Tags. A tag is a fixed name for one commit, used to mark releases. A branch moves when you commit; a tag stays where you put it. Create. Lightweight tag: git tag v zero dot one. Annotated tag: git tag dash a v one dot zero dash m First release. What is stored. Lightweight tag: A name that points at a commit. Annotated tag: A tag object with tagger, date and message. git show. Lightweight tag: The commit only. Annotated tag: Tag details, then the commit. git describe. Lightweight tag: Ignored by default. Annotated tag: Used.

2.title: Tags, continued
2.text: Tags. git tag lists names alphabetically and git tag dash l v one. filters them. git tag dash d name deletes a tag and leaves the commits alone. To tag an older commit, add its hash: git tag dash a v one dot zero hash. git describe names the current commit from the nearest annotated tag. The result v one dot zero to two g seven zero two seven seven f seven means two commits after v one.zero, then a g and the short hash. On the tagged commit itself it prints just v one dot zero. git describe the tags flag also counts lightweight tags.

2.title: Tags, continued
2.text: Tags. A plain git push does not send tags. You push a tag by name with git push origin v one dot zero (module seven). Tip: Use annotated tags for releases. They record who tagged and why, and git describe works with them.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Bob runs git branch dash d experiment and Git prints "the branch 'experiment' is not fully merged". What does this mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The branch has commits that are not in the current branch. The safe delete refuses when deleting would lose commits, and dash D is the forced version.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Ada's old guide says git checkout dash b feature slash cart. Which modern command does the same thing? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git switch dash c feature slash cart, which creates it and moves. git switch dash c creates the branch and switches to it in one step.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. git status says "head detached at v one.zero". Cy has made two commits there and wants to keep them. What should he run before leaving? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: git switch dash c rescue, so a branch points at the commits. A new branch keeps the commits reachable, while switching away leaves them with no pointer.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Ada has an uncommitted edit to cart.txt on main. She runs git switch feature slash search, where cart.txt differs. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Git refuses to switch and keeps her edit where it is. Git refuses when the switch would overwrite local changes, so she stays on main and loses nothing.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. The team needs a release marker that records who made it and why, and that git describe can use. What should they create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: git tag dash a v one dot zero dash m First release, an annotated tag. An annotated tag stores the tagger, date and message, and git describe uses annotated tags by default.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Cy tagged v one.zero and ran git push origin main. A teammate fetches and cannot see the tag. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A plain push does not send tags, so Cy must push the tag. Tags are pushed by name, for instance with git push origin v one dot zero.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does git switch - do? Answer: It returns to the previous branch. Question two. Which flag deletes a branch even when it is unmerged? Answer: dash D, as in git branch dash D name. Question three. What does git branch dash v v show beyond the names? Answer: The last commit and the upstream branch with ahead and behind counts.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a detached head? Answer: head points at a commit, such as a hash or a tag, instead of a branch. Question five. Which command names a commit from the nearest annotated tag? Answer: git describe. Question six. Which command renames the current branch? Answer: git branch dash m new name.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. List and create: git branch, git branch name; a slash is allowed in names. Switch: git switch name, git switch dash c name, git switch -; older: git checkout. Uncommitted edits: They travel along, or Git refuses if they would be overwritten. Rename: git branch dash m old new, or git branch dash m new for the current branch. Delete: dash d refuses unmerged work; dash D forces; you cannot delete the current branch. Inspect: git branch dash v v shows the last commit and the upstream; the merged flag, the no merged flag. Detached head: head holds a hash; rescue commits with git switch dash c name. Tags: Lightweight is a name; annotated has a message; git tag dash d; git describe.
